newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian post-privatisation fund ready to invest.
newsitem.headline: Romanian post-privatisation fund ready to invest.

text.p: A Romanian post-privatisation fund with 44 million Ecus ($55.5 million) at its disposal said on Wednesday it hoped to make its first investment early next year.
"We hope to have the first investment approved before end-January," fund general manager Robert Luke told journalists.
The fund is intended to secure private equity financing for small and medium-sized companies in the private sector where long-term credits and risk capital resources are limited.

Money for the National Privatisation Agency post-privatisation foundation came from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development -- 25 million Ecus -- and the European Union's Phare programme -- 15 million Ecus.
Spanish investment company GED Capital Development, the manager of the fund, also contributed 4.0 million Ecus.
"We'll be interested in companies with at least 51 percent of shares privately owned and the money we'll give will be to increase capital rather than buy existing shares," Luke said.
Investment would not focus on distinct sectors but on companies which have potential for growth. The fund's exposure in a company will not exceed 3.0 million Ecus.
The fund plans to work closely with foreign funds.
"At least a dozen funds in the U.K. and on Wall Street have dedicated half the money they raised to Eastern Europe. They could put their money on top of our money," Luke said.
The fund already has a portfolio of around 80 companies.
"We've been impressed by the quality of companies and of management teams. They can compete profitably in Romania and soon in other European countries," Luke said.
The private sector, almost non-existent before Romania ended communism in 1989, is forecast to account for 60 percent of the gross domestic product this year, up from 45 percent in 1995.
